headline: Showers end tonight, then dry, sunny, frosty mornings through Monday; uncertain midweek rain, then warmer, lower-70s weather by Friday.
summary: As of Saturday evening, a slow-moving low pressure system is leaving the region. A few leftover showers near central and eastern King and Pierce counties should end tonight, and isolated patches of fog are possible overnight, mainly in fog-prone spots of the southwest interior. Dry air from the northeast and clear skies will make nights cold, with lows from the 30s to mid 40s tonight and mostly in the 30s Sunday night. Frost is likely early Sunday in the southern Cascade foothills and valleys and south of the Olympics, and more widespread early Monday, including most areas south of Seattle, along Hood Canal and on the north coast. Frost Advisories cover both mornings (midnight to 8 AM Sunday, and midnight Sunday night to 8 AM Monday). Sunday highs should be in the mid 50s to lower 60s, and Monday highs in the upper 50s to mid 60s under mostly clear to sunny skies, which is near normal. Clouds increase Tuesday as a weak atmospheric river (a narrow stream of moisture) aims mostly at British Columbia. Rain chances rise Tuesday along the coast and over higher terrain, then more broadly across western Washington late Tuesday into Wednesday, but forecasters are unsure where the moisture will go and many computer model runs keep western Washington mostly dry. High pressure returns Thursday, bringing warmer, drier weather, with highs reaching the lower 70s by Friday. By the weekend the high pressure ridge could break down, bringing some rain and cooler temperatures, though how long the warm, dry weather lasts is uncertain.
changes: Earlier discussions called for rain chances Tuesday night and Wednesday and a warm-up starting Wednesday night. By afternoon, forecasters instead had rain chances starting Tuesday on the coast and in the mountains, warmth returning Thursday, and a possible return of rain and cooler weather by the weekend, with midweek rain described as much less certain.
